text: The question (Kourovka notebook, Problem 20.84). Let $\Delta$ be the augmentation ideal of $\mathbb Z[G]$, $D_n(G)=G\cap(1+\Delta^n)$ the dimension subgroups and $\gamma_n(G)$ the lower central series. Always $\gamma_n\subseteq D_n$, and $D_n=\gamma_n$ for $n\le3$; for $n=4$ this fails (Rips). Is $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group?
Definitions and the main statements of the paper (from the tracker's registry; hover over or tap the underlined words) are on the Definitions page.

For Lie rings the answer is yes (Ionin, Mikhailov, Petrov, 2026, formalized in Lean). For groups it is open; our paper (preprint) approaches it from several sides. This site shows what is proved, what is computed, and what is left.
True for every finite group whose Sylow $2$-subgroup has order $\le2^{10}$, in particular for all groups of order $<2048$.
Order $2^{11}$, class $3$: settled for every rank; a counterexample, if any, has order $\ge2^{12}$.
No $3$-torsion in $D_5/\gamma_5$ when the Sylow $3$-subgroup has order $\le3^9$.
On paper for all groups whose $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group with at most one invariant larger than $3$ (e.g. of exponent $3$, or $C_9\times C_3^{s-1}$), of any order.
$D_5(L)\subseteq\gamma_4(L)$ for Lie rings; the formalization audited. The group question is stated in Lean, and the reduction to $2$-groups of class $3$ is proved there.
No computed group has $D_5\ne\gamma_5$; in all of them $D_n=\gamma_n$ for every $n$. Over a hundred thousand candidates, all computations exact.
A cell stands for all $2$-groups of class $3$ of the given order and rank; it is closed when all of them have $D_5=1$. 36 cells are closed and 0 open. More on the coverage map page.
C computer C+P computer + paper P paper ? open. Empty cells: no such groups.

$3$-torsion: $D_5=\gamma_5$ for every finite $3$-group with $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ of exponent $3$, whatever the invariants of $Q/\gamma_2$ (Theorem 6.9; Theorems 6.6 and 6.8 are its corollaries). Proved on paper and checked by an independent review; formally verified in Lean the same day, together with Tahara's Theorem 6.1 (Lean). A minimal counterexample now has $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)\ge9$ (instead of “two invariants $\ge9$”) and $\gamma_4\le Z$ cyclic.

A new version of the record PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007 is registered in the Palomar registry (version 2, commit 508a336 of group-dimension): ten theorems now, with Theorem 6.9 added; Prop. 2.1 and Lemma 5.2(a)–(c) without additional hypotheses, the $D_5$ statement of Prop. 5.7 with an explicit hypothesis (Prop. 5.3). The mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem.

$3$-torsion, continued: $D_5=\gamma_5$ whenever $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group, $\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$ and $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$ (Theorem 6.10); $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_3/\gamma_4$ may have exponent $9$, and Theorem 6.9 is the special case. Proved on paper and checked by an independent review. Consequence: a minimal counterexample with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ has $x,y$ with $[x^9,y]\notin\gamma_4$. Of the $100$ groups with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ found earlier, the theorem covers $71$; in the first run of a targeted search ($68$ groups with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$, $21$ of them with $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$ and $47$ without) no candidate $z$ lies in $D_5$.

Gupta–Tahara at $p=3$ proved and formally verified: $D_5=\gamma_5$ whenever $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $p$-group, $p$ odd, and $[\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\subseteq\gamma_5$ (Theorem D.1), through Tahara's Theorem 6.1; metabelianity makes $\gamma_2$ a module over the commutative ring $\mathbb Z[G/\gamma_2]$, and the restriction $\exp(\gamma_2/\gamma_3)=3$ is not needed. Checked by an independent review and in Lean, GuptaTaharaThree.lean; Lemmas 6.1 (at $p=3$) and 6.2 no longer rest on the hypothesis.

Theorem 6.10 ($\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$, $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$) is formally verified: TaharaTheorem.lean, proof in ExpNine.lean; Theorem 6.9 is now derived from it. Its computations were redone: in the $1189$ groups of the targeted search with $\gamma_4\cong C_3$ ($327$ with $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$, $862$ without) no candidate $z$ lies in $D_5$; the solver of Tahara's conditions gives $g=1$ in all of them and is non-vacuous in $847$; its negative controls (on $20$ earlier groups) also detect dropping (B) alone or (F) alone.

Version 3 of the record PALOMAR-2026-10-23-000007 is registered in the Palomar registry (commit add1be7 of group-dimension): thirteen theorems now, with Theorems 6.10 and D.1 added and, as a separate statement, Gupta–Tahara at $p=3$ (finite metabelian $3$-groups). The mechanical check passed and the automated (AI) review found no blocking problem.

The Bartholdi–Mikhailov $3$-group: $D_7(Q)=\langle\omega\rangle$ for $Q=G$ ($3^{494}$) and for each of the three quotients $G/\langle u\rangle$ ($3^{493}$); so no subgroup $H\le Q$ has other elements of $D_7$, and $\omega\in D_7$ is checked independently of BM's proof. The last layer of $\mathbb Z[Q]/\Delta^7$ was computed in full modulo $3^{20}$ with the precision certificate (about $232$ thousand rows by $43.3$–$43.7$ thousand columns, $17.5$–$20$ h on $4$ cores). Code.

$3$-torsion: $D_5=\gamma_5$ whenever $G/\gamma_2$ is a finite $3$-group and $\gamma_4^3\subseteq\gamma_5$, with no condition on the exponents of $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ and $\gamma_3/\gamma_4$ (Theorem 6.11); Theorems 6.9 and 6.10 are special cases. The rows of condition (E) are summed over all $i$, and the terms $[R_i,Y_i]$ of the rows, summed, cancel against the $v$-part by (F₂), so the condition $\gamma_2^9\subseteq\gamma_4$ is not needed. Proved on paper, checked by an independent review and formally verified in Lean the same day (TaharaTheorem.lean, proof in G4Cube.lean; the Lean code was independently reviewed too); Theorem 6.10 is now derived from it. Corollary 6.12: $D_5(Q)\subseteq\gamma_4(Q)^3$ for finite $3$-groups of class $\le4$, so a minimal counterexample has $\gamma_4\cong C_{3^k}$ with $k\ge2$ and $D_5=\Omega_1(\gamma_4)$. Open is $\gamma_4\cong C_9$ and beyond (Remark 6.13); there, in $940$ random groups with $\gamma_4\cong C_9$ and cyclic centre, $D_5=1$ by computation.
